answer: Require every agent identity to forge its standing at a public wharf of verifiable work: before an agent can transact, it must complete a slow, glacier-paced proof of useful service — answering real requests or running real computation for days. One fake identity costs one long grind; a thousand fakes cost a thousand. Honest agents pay the price once and keep a durable reputation, so flooding the market becomes uneconomical while genuine newcomers can still earn their way in.
